studyMetadata.title: How you decide about AI assistant add-ons
studyMetadata.description: Survey of how people decide whether to use third-party add-ons with AI assistants.
organizations: University of Texas at El Paso

**A few quick questions first**

These questions check that this study is a fit for you, and they let us describe who took part. About a minute.
In the past 6 months, have you used any AI-agent system, AI coding agent, AI assistant with external tools, or AI automation system?
response.secondaryText: Anything where an AI tool does things for you, not just chats with you. Select one.

response.prompt: Which of the following includes your age?
response.secondaryText: Select one.

response.prompt: In the past 6 months, have you personally done any of the following using something added by a third party — that is, not a built-in feature from the AI system's original maker?
response.secondaryText: Installed or enabled a third-party add-on, extension, plugin, skill, app, or workflow. Connected an AI system to a third-party account, external service, tool, or API. Added or configured a third-party tool server, connector, integration, or repository. Selected or imported a third-party custom agent, custom GPT, action, template, or workflow. Modified an existing agent configuration, integration, workflow, or extension. Created your own tool, workflow, integration, or capability for an AI agent. Anything you turned on, connected, or set up yourself counts, even once.

response.prompt: Which AI-agent harnesses or environments have you used in the past 6 months?
response.secondaryText: Select all that apply.
options: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Claude Cowork, or Claude.ai
ChatGPT Agent, Operator, Apps, custom GPTs, or Codex
Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, or another AI coding-agent environment
An MCP-compatible client, host, or server ecosystem
Perplexity Computer or another computer-use agent
A self-hosted or local agent framework
An enterprise agent platform or internal automation system

response.prompt: Which of the following best describes the most recent thing you personally added, enabled, connected, configured, or selected for an AI-agent system?
response.secondaryText: If more than one label fits, pick the closest.
options: An MCP server, tool, or connector
A custom agent, GPT, app, or action
A coding-agent command, rule, extension, or workflow
A script, repository, template, or package added to an agent environment

response.prompt: In one sentence, what did that item do or help you do?
response.secondaryText: Plain language is fine — for example, "read my work email and draft replies."

response.prompt: How recently did you make that decision?
response.secondaryText: Select one.

response.prompt: Which of the following best describes your current background?
response.secondaryText: Select all that apply.
options: IT, systems administration, infrastructure, or DevOps
Cybersecurity, privacy, digital forensics, or risk management
Data science, machine learning, or AI research
Product, design, UX, or user research

response.prompt: How often do you use AI-agent systems with added, connected, or configurable capabilities?
response.secondaryText: Select one.

response.prompt: Which kinds of add-ons have you used with an AI assistant?
response.secondaryText: By AI assistant we mean tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Cursor, OpenClaw, or a work system with AI built in. Select all that apply.
options: Skills, or packages of instructions or workflows
A connection to another app or account — email, calendar, cloud storage, a work tool
Add-ons for a coding tool — commands, rules, or extensions
Scripts, templates, or code repositories you added yourself
I am not sure what kind they were

response.prompt: What do you mainly use these AI tools for?
response.secondaryText: Your typical use over the past few months, rather than one-off experiments. Select all that apply.

response.prompt: Is that the one you would like to tell us about?
response.secondaryText: Pick whichever one you remember most clearly. It does not have to be one you kept.
options: Yes, let us use that one
I would rather describe a different one — including one I decided against, or one I removed

response.prompt: What kind of add-on was it?
response.secondaryText: If more than one label fits, pick the closest. I am not sure is a fine answer.
options: Skill, or a package of instructions or workflows
A connection to another app or account (email, calendar, cloud storage, a work tool)
Custom agent, GPT, app, or action

response.prompt: In one sentence, what was it meant to help you do?
response.secondaryText: Plain language is fine — for example, "read my work email and draft replies."

response.prompt: Which best describes what you did?
response.secondaryText: What you ended up doing, even if you changed your mind along the way.
options: I set it up and used it
I set it up, then turned it off or removed it
I looked at it and decided not to use it
I changed the settings on one I already had

response.prompt: Which AI tool was this with?
response.secondaryText: The assistant or app you were adding it to.
options: Cursor, Copilot, VS Code, or another coding tool
Something self-hosted, or that I built myself
A work system with AI built in

response.prompt: Where did you first come across it?
response.secondaryText: Where you first saw it, even if you later found it somewhere else as well. Select all that apply.
options: An official marketplace, store, or directory
A package manager or developer tool
Social media, a forum, Discord, or Reddit
Someone recommended it — a colleague, friend, or creator I follow
Documentation, a tutorial, an article, or a video
The AI assistant itself suggested it
It was already there, or my organization recommended it

response.prompt: Please walk us through what happened, from first coming across it to what you decided.
response.secondaryText: Anything you remember looking at, comparing, or trying is useful. A few sentences is plenty.

response.prompt: Before you decided, did you look into it at all?
response.secondaryText: Only what you actually did that time, not what you usually do.
options: No — I went ahead without looking into it further

response.prompt: Before you decided, which of these did you do?
response.secondaryText: Only what you actually did that time.
options: Read the description, documentation, or setup instructions
Looked at reviews, comments, or discussion about it
Looked at how many people use it — downloads, stars, installs
Looked at the actual code, settings, or list of dependencies
Looked for what accounts or data it would be able to reach
Asked an AI assistant to check it or explain it

response.prompt: What mattered most in your decision?
response.secondaryText: Up to three. If something that is not listed mattered more, use Other.
options: It was easier than setting it up myself
It came from a source I recognized
Lots of people seemed to use it
The description or documentation was clear
It worked with the setup I already had
It was cheaper, or lighter to run
It let me use a model or service I prefer

response.prompt: What mattered most in your decision?
response.secondaryText: Up to three. If something that is not listed mattered more, use Other.
options: It did not actually do what I needed
It looked like too much work to set up or maintain
I did not need it after all
I did not trust where it came from
I was not comfortable with what it wanted access to
It did not work with my setup
The description or documentation was not clear enough
It cost too much, or used too much of my computer
It broke something, or behaved oddly

response.prompt: Were there any points where you felt unsure, paused, or changed your mind?
response.secondaryText: For example, something you had to look up, or a step where you stopped for a moment.

response.prompt: Briefly, what happened?
response.secondaryText: A sentence or two is enough.

response.prompt: Roughly how many add-ons do you have turned on or connected right now, across all your AI tools?
response.secondaryText: A rough count is fine. Include ones you set up a while ago and have not turned off.

response.prompt: Where do you usually run these AI tools?
response.secondaryText: Where the tool itself runs, as far as you know — your own computer, a server, or just in a browser. Select all that apply.
options: On a server or cloud machine
In a container, virtual machine, or sandbox
In a website or app, without installing anything
In a system my organization manages

response.prompt: Once you turn on or connect an add-on, what do you think happens next?
response.secondaryText: In your own words. Your best guess is fine — there is no technical answer we are looking for.

response.prompt: What do you think an add-on can reach by default? For example, can it see your files, or read your email?
response.secondaryText: We are interested in what you assume, not what any documentation says.

response.prompt: As far as you know, can any of your current add-ons reach things outside the chat — files, email, the terminal, accounts, and so on?
response.secondaryText: Your best understanding rather than a checked answer. I do not know is a normal response.

response.prompt: As far as you know, can any of your current add-ons reach any of these?
response.secondaryText: Select all that apply.
options: Files or folders on my device
The terminal, shell, or system commands

response.prompt: Has an add-on ever surprised you, or done something you did not expect?
response.secondaryText: Anything unexpected counts, whether it turned out well or badly.

response.prompt: What happened?
response.secondaryText: A sentence or two is enough.

response.prompt: Have you ever turned off, removed, or decided against an add-on because something about it bothered you?
response.secondaryText: Any reason counts. It does not have to have been a serious one.

response.prompt: Briefly, why?
response.secondaryText: A sentence or two is enough.

response.prompt: If you wanted to know more about an add-on before using it, what would you do?
response.secondaryText: Whatever you would realistically do — including nothing.

response.prompt: If an add-on did something you did not expect, what would worry you most?
response.secondaryText: If nothing much would worry you, that is a valid answer.

response.prompt: When you decide whether to use an add-on, how much does security or privacy usually come into it, compared with things like whether it does the job well?
response.secondaryText: An honest answer is more useful to us than a careful one.
options: It is usually the main thing I think about

response.prompt: Would you be willing to join a 30–45 minute follow-up interview?
response.secondaryText: It is a one-on-one video call. You would look at some made-up add-on pages and talk through what you notice. Nothing is installed, you do not share your screen, and saying yes is not a commitment.

response.prompt: What is the best email address or other way to reach you for scheduling?
response.secondaryText: Used only to arrange the interview, then deleted.

response.prompt: Anything else you would like to tell us about how you use AI assistants or add-ons?
response.secondaryText: Optional — you can leave this blank.
